about: READ-ONLY: renders what `expand-instance-volume` WOULD do to one instance's PersistentVolumeClaim, and does nothing (infra/forge/expand-instance-volume.sh --plan <namespace> <pvc> <size>; backlog ebbb923f, incident d3c0a67c). It runs every bound the write runs — an instances.toml namespace; a Bound claim with no expansion in flight; a driver.longhorn.io class with allowVolumeExpansion true; a healthy Longhorn volume that is this claim's at the claim's size; a whole-GiB size that grows, at most 2x and at most the script's 100 GiB ceiling — and, for EVERY disk holding a replica of the volume, both halves of Longhorn v1.11.3's admission check (CheckReplicasSizeExpansion), with required = replicas-on-the-disk x growth and ProvisionedLimit = (storageMaximum - storageReserved) x storage-over-provisioning-percentage / 100: first ValidateDiskAvailableForExpansion on the disk's physical space (physicalUsed = storageMaximum - storageAvailable - storageReserved; physicalUsed + required <= ProvisionedLimit, and storageMaximum - (physicalUsed + required) at or above the storage-minimal-available-percentage floor), then IsSchedulableToDisk on the ledger (ScheduledTotal = storageScheduled + required <= ProvisionedLimit, storageAvailable above the floor), read from nodes.longhorn.io (the replica's spec.diskID is the disk's diskUUID) and settings.longhorn.io. The physical half was added after adversarial review adc832e2 found a growth the ledger admitted and the disk could not hold; it reads the live storageAvailable, so it is judged on stderr at both renders, while the signed size ceiling is the scheduling-ledger fit only, in whole GiB (shared infra/lib/longhorn-ledger.sh, backlog 64e00b78). The current physical fit is printed on stderr and rechecked before any write; admissible changes in live free space leave the plan bytes and hash unchanged. A size the webhook would refuse is refused here in the webhook's own figures, naming the largest size that fits; one that fits prints the plan: the claim, class, volume, the size before and after, the bounds, the largest ledger-admitted size and the largest one run grants subject to the live physical check, the one compare-and-set patch, the read-back, every replica, and every replica disk's sum. No clock and no live free space in the bytes (storageAvailable rides stderr); its sha256 is printed on stderr as `plan-sha256:`, and that hash is what David's passkey signs (design 17835005 q1). Every read goes through the forge's ops_kubectl door; a read that could not look is CANNOT ANSWER (exit 1), never a plan. Any refusal renders no plan.
